# SSH bastion test fixture

Throwaway credentials for the SSH tunnel tests. **None of this material is secret, and none of it
grants access to anything** - the keys are generated for this directory, live only inside a
container built at test time, and are regenerated by anyone who wants to.

A secret scanner will flag `test_key` and `test_key_passphrase` as private keys. That is expected,
and matches the already-committed PEM material under `internal/modules/backups/e2e/postgresql/testdata/`.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Dockerfile` | Alpine + OpenSSH bastion. Creates the `testuser` account and sets its password. |
| `sshd_config` | Permits TCP forwarding and adds a second listener on 2222. |
| `authorized_keys` | Public halves of both keys below. |
| `test_key` | Passphrase-less ed25519 private key, for the public-key auth test. |
| `test_key_passphrase` | ed25519 private key protected with the passphrase `testpassphrase`. |

Account baked into the image: `testuser` / `testpassword`.

## Why sshd listens on 2222

The tunnel tests forward to port 2222 rather than 22. Port 2222 is never published to the host, so
a forwarder that stopped tunnelling and dialled the host loopback instead cannot accidentally reach
a developer's or CI runner's own sshd and pass. `Test_TargetPort_WithoutTheTunnel_IsUnreachableFromTheHost`
pins that property.

## Regenerating

```sh
cd backend/internal/lib/testcontainers/testdata/ssh_bastion
rm -f test_key test_key_passphrase authorized_keys

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -C "databasus-sshtunnel-test" -f test_key
mv test_key.pub authorized_keys

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "testpassphrase" -C "databasus-sshtunnel-test-passphrase" -f test_key_passphrase
cat test_key_passphrase.pub >> authorized_keys
rm test_key_passphrase.pub
```

The passphrase is asserted verbatim in `forwarder_test.go`; changing it means changing the test.
